followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors:

**Task type:** This is a creative/generative writing task with meaningful latitude — choosing replacement words to deepen a poem's meaning. Avocet self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work and prefers well-specified extraction/reformatting tasks, while this query is squarely in the creative latitude zone Avocet dislikes.

**Capability:** Plover scores higher across essentially every relevant metric — Creative Generation (84.7 vs 82.7, though within tie range), and notably stronger Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 83.2) and general benchmarks, which track the kind of nuanced, quality-sensitive open-ended response this request demands. The user is explicitly demanding high effort ("actually try this time"), so the model with the stronger general capability profile is the better fit.

**Preference fit:** Routing creative work away from a model that self-reports disliking it (Avocet) toward one with no such aversion (Plover) is the cleaner match — even though documentation notes preference is dissociated from quality, there's no downside to honoring the fit here.

The hostile/demanding tone of the user isn't really a distasteful-content issue, so Plover's moderation specialization wasn't the deciding factor — its overall capability edge plus the creative-task fit was.
